observed_failure: A Git bundle produced by an actual depth-1 shallow checkout can reference an intentionally absent parent; fetching that bundle into a normal empty repository fails because the receiver requests missing history.
counterhypothesis: The bundle alone is sufficient to reconstruct exact provenance regardless of whether the source checkout is shallow.
repair: Stage v5 records whether the exact source checkout is shallow. If shallow, the isolated receiver writes the exact source HEAD to .git/shallow before bundle fetch, preserving that commit as the intentional artificial root; non-shallow receivers create no shallow boundary.
normal_regression_observations: canonical raw-Git-tree TAR byte-identical across full and depth-1 source checkouts
depth-1 receiver remains shallow at exactly source HEAD
upstream_semantic_basis: Git repository-layout documentation defines commits listed in $GIT_DIR/shallow as artificial roots; the repair binds the receiver to the source checkout's actual shallow boundary instead of inventing parent history.
promotion_discriminator: An actually-started exact-head Vercel build-internal Sandbox must prove shallow-safe Stage-v5 provenance and then pass the existing DENY_ALL Bytes-v2 + twin one-file EntityOS matrix.
